title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Jordan Kim
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token costs and operator effort by shipping an automated defaults/autotune pipeline that tunes batching, KV-prefix caching, and quantization profiles for common workload classes, while exposing unit-economics visibility in the Console. This PR implements: 1) autotune service that recommends batching/caching defaults based on observed latency/throughput distributions; 2) quantization profile store and a runtime switch that safely falls back to full-precision variants; 3) Unit Economics API + Console panel to show projected cost/throughput impact of recommended profiles. The description below is intentionally compact but contains the full rollout plan and testing notes. Changeset highlights: - new autotune service (runtime/autotune) with offline and online modes - quant profiles persisted in ops/quant/profiles.yaml with compatibility metadata - console API + frontend for unit-economics (redwood/console/*) - migration: existing per-customer batching/caching configs will be honored; new customers get autotune defaults after opt-in. Checklist: [x] API + runtime proto and implementation [x] Quant profile format + migration script [x] Console UI and API endpoints [x] Unit tests + e2e tests [x] Performance benchmarks (internal) [x] Docs/upgrade notes (docs/cost-optimization.md) Rollout plan: 1) behind feature flag (autotune.enabled=false) on main for first canary customers; 2) run pilot with 3 internal customers for 2 weeks; 3) enable opt-in in Console UI and gather signals; 4) gradual auto-rollout with 1% increments and circuit breaker on latency/regression alerts. Backwards compatibility & safety: - All autotune changes are opt-in by default. - Quant profiles include a compatibility matrix (min-runtime-version, fallback-model) and runtime will fallback automatically on any runtime error. - Batching/caching defaults are suggestions surfaced to ops and require explicit apply unless customer enables auto-apply. Testing & metrics: - unit + integration tests added (redwood/tests/) - synthetic perf harnesses used to validate latency p99 under mixed workloads - added metrics: autotune.recommendation.count, uecon.estimated_cost_delta, quant.profile_applied.count - CI: lint, unit, integration, e2e (see ci_summary) Migration notes: migration script converts any legacy batching YAML to the new autotune format. If migration fails for a customer, the system leaves their configs unchanged and writes a migration error to audit logs. Related: Linear ENG-3241, PM-128. See docs link: /docs/cost-optimization.md.
